entities.text:
United India Insurance Company ... vs Smt. Sithale Prabhavathi
And 5 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The appellant insurance company - respondent no.2 has filed the present appeal aggrieved by the order and decree dated 03.07.2007 passed in O.P.No.1063 of 2002 by the I Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal at Nizamabad.

entities.text: I Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal at Nizamabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Having heard Mr. Mohan Krishna, learned counsel for the appellant insurance company and Ms.
Swathi, representing Mr. K. Raghuveer Reddy, learned counsel for the respondents claimants,
perused the entire material on record.
3. The claim petition was filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.10,00,000/- on account of the death of deceased in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 08.05.2002.
The deceased was private medical practitioner and earning an amount of Rs.10,000/- per month.
The Tribunal, as there was no evidence, has taken Rs.5,000/- as income of the deceased and granted compensation of an amount of Rs.7,00,000/-.

4. Learned counsel for the insurance company submitted that the offending vehicle was hazardous vehicle and deceased was not LK,J having license to drive the hazardous vehicle and in that case, the Tribunal ought not to have fasten the liability on the insurance company.
He also submitted that for the age of 32 applying multiplier 17 was wrong.
The Court below ought to have deducted 1/4th of the income towards personal expenses of the deceased, but, however has deducted 1/3rd of the income.
It is also submitted that as there are 5 dependants instead of deducting 1/4th, the Tribunal has deducted 1/3rd.
He also submits that the award passed by the Tribunal was wrong.

5. Learned counsel for the claimants submitted that though the claimants have neither filed independent appeal nor cross objections, still the insurance company is questioning the quantum of compensation and the claimants can as well seek for enhancement of the compensation before this Court.
6. Learned counsel for the claimants submits that according to them the crime vehicle is hazardous vehicle and the deceased was not having license to drive the said hazardous vehicle.
She also submits that the Court below has dealt with this issue and observed that the driver of the crime vehicle is not having valid driving license to drive the hazardous vehicle.

The Court below LK,J United India Insurance Company ... vs Smt. Sithale Prabhavathi And 5 Others on 15 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45780024/
1 observed that as per the driving license issued by the Transport Authorities, Nalgonda, the driver had valid driving license to drive Heavy Transport Vehicle i.e., HGV, HPV and also having appsv Badge and even according to the MVI report also there is no mention that the crime vehicle is a hazardous vehicle.
7.

entities.text: LK,J United India Insurance Company ... vs Smt. Sithale Prabhavathi And 5 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The contention of the learned counsel for the insurance company has no locus standi.
8. Then coming to the aspect of compensation, though it was claimed by the claimants that the deceased was earning an amount of Rs.10,000/-, as there was no evidence the Court has taken Rs.5,000/.
9. This Court is of the view that as there was no evidence, the Court below has rightly taken Rs.5,000/-.

Hence, this Court is inclined to consider the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.5,000/-.
10.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi 1 held that while considering the compensation in cases of death, the future prospects of the self employed shall also 2017 (6) 170 (SC) LK,J be considered.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Having regard to the age and occupation as self- employed, if 40 percent of the income is included as future prospects, the monthly income would come to Rs.7,000/-.
As the dependants are five members, 1/4th of the income has to be deducted towards personal expenditure, as per law laid down in Smt. Sarla Varma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation2.

entities.text: Smt. Sarla Varma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, the annual contribution of the deceased to the claimants would be of Rs.63,000/-
(7000-1750X12).
As per Schedule II of the Act, if the said annual contribution arrived is multiplied with relevant multiplier to the age of the deceased i.e.16, the total amount comes to Rs.10,08,000/-.
The claimants are entitled for the said amount under the head of loss of dependency.

11. As regards the consortium to be paid to the dependants of the deceased is concerned, each one is entitled to Rs.44,000/- towards consortium as decided by the Hon'ble Apex court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others 3 .

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others 3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: With regard to the funeral expenses and loss of estate, the claimants are entitled to Rs.33,000/-.

Further, under the heads of attendant benefits, transport, extra nourishment and legal (2009) 6 S.C.C. 121 2017 ACJ 2700 LK,J expenses,
this Court is inclined to grant an amount of Rs.10,000/-.
12.

In the light of the above mentioned discussion, the claimants are entitled to the following amounts:
 Head Compensation awarded  (1) Loss of dependency Rs.10,08,000  (2) Funeral expenses and Rs.33,000  Loss of Estate  (3) Loss of spousal consortium Rs.44,000 for 1st appellant United India Insurance Company ... vs Smt. Sithale Prabhavathi And 5 Others on 15 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45780024/
2  (4) Loss of parental consortium Rs.1,32,000 for 2nd, 3rd  and 4th Appellants  (5) Loss of filial consortium Rs.44,000 for 5th appellant  (6) Legal expenses Rs.10,000 Total compensation awarded Rs.12,71,000/-
13.

In the result, the Motor Accident Miscellaneous Appeal of the insurance company is dismissed enhancing the compensation amount awarded by the court below from Rs.7,00,000/- to Rs.12,71,000/- as hereunder:
(a) The enhanced amount shall carry interest at 7.5% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realization.
LK,J
(b) The claimants shall pay the court fee on the enhanced amount of compensation.
(c) The insurance company shall deposit the amount within a period of (8) weeks from the date of receipt of copy of judgment.
On such deposit, claimants are entitled to withdraw the entire amount without furnishing the security.
(d) Amounts shall be apportioned in terms of the ratio decided by the Tribunal in the Award.

Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
